meta.title: Shramko Motor Autostart — spin a motor on power-up with Betaflight, no receiver
meta.ogTitle: Shramko Motor Autostart — a Betaflight motor driver you configure in the browser
meta.description: Betaflight 2025.12.1 firmware that starts a brushless motor by itself: battery in, delay, smooth linear ramp, hold — no receiver. Set the delay, ramp, throttle, gusts, run time and LiPo cut-off over USB, right in your browser.
meta.ogAlt: A throttle ramp curve and a motor rotor on a dark background

hero.eyebrow: Free Betaflight firmware + setup in your browser
hero.sub: Spins a motor by itself when you plug in the battery. No receiver, no remote.
hero.lead: Built to blow rain off a 360° camera lens. Put the firmware on an HGLRC F405 board once, then choose the wait, power and run time here — in Chrome or Edge on Windows.
hero.by: By Andrii Shramko — built for a storm-chasing 360° camera case
cfg.title: Configurator
cfg.lead: Settings and live data stay between your browser and the board.
cfg.fallbackTitle: The configurator needs JavaScript and Web Serial
cfg.fallback: It runs in Chrome, Edge or Opera on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS, and in Firefox 151+ (it asks once for a site permission). Android: Chrome 148+ on phones whose Android supports USB serial — try it. iPhone and iPad cannot do it: their browsers have neither Web Serial nor WebUSB.
cfg.fallbackCli_html: No suitable browser? Every setting is also in the Betaflight CLI: get autostart, set autostart_throttle = 80, save. Names, ranges and defaults: settings reference.
cfg.stub: The live configurator will appear here. Until then, use the Betaflight CLI (see Install below).
install.title: Put the firmware on the board
install.lead: About five minutes, once per board. You need the board, a USB data cable and Chrome or Edge on a computer.
install.s1_html: Get the file for your board from the latest release on GitHub. Ready build: HGLRC F405 8S V2 — betaflight_2025.12.1_STM32F405_HGLRC_F405_S8_autostart.hex (Betaflight board_name HGLRC_F405_S8).
install.s2_html: Before you flash or connect anything, remove the propeller or blower wheel. With this firmware the motor starts by itself 10 seconds after a battery is plugged in. More: Risks and safety.
install.s3t: Flash it with the Betaflight App
install.s3_html: Open app.betaflight.com in Chrome or Edge and plug the board in by USB. Then Firmware Flasher → Load Firmware [Local] → pick the .hex → Flash Firmware.
install.dfu_html: Windows is missing the bootloader driver. Run the ImpulseRC Driver Fixer (one click), or use Zadig: pick STM32 BOOTLOADER and install WinUSB. Then flash again.
install.s4t: Close the Betaflight App, then connect
install.s4_html: Only one program can use the board at a time. The first start after flashing resets the settings once — that is expected. Then go to step 2 and press Connect.
install.moreT: Another board, older versions, going back to stock
install.other_html: Build it from source: copy the board's config.h from betaflight/config into configs/<BOARD>/, add #define USE_AUTOSTART and run the Docker build — see README → Build from source.
install.ver_html: v1.1.0 (current): delay, ramp, throttle and its limit, run time, random gusts, battery cut-off, outputs, battery gate, button and RC switch. v1.0.0 boards connect too but show only the settings they have — update to get the rest. To go back, flash …_stock.hex from the release: the same Betaflight without the module.
how.title: How it works
how.lead: Plug in the battery: the board waits, speeds the motor up in a straight line, then holds it or adds gusts — until the run time is over or the battery is low.
how.m3t: Max deviation from a straight line
how.mNote_html: Measured on a real HGLRC F405 8S V2 over USB with the factory settings (10 s wait, 10 s speed-up to 15 %). Raw data and test tools: README → Verified on hardware.
how.techT: Technical details: states and setting names
how.techLead: The module writes the throttle where the Betaflight Motors tab writes it while disarmed, so the DShot/PWM output, ESC arming and telemetry stay stock. A 50 Hz task runs five states:
how.s1_html: The board measures the battery on its B pin. From autostart_vbat_min (6.0 V) on, the battery counts as plugged in. On battery-only power that is the moment of power-on.
how.s2_html: autostart_delay seconds (10). Meanwhile the ESC gets stop frames — always at least 3 s — so it arms on zero throttle.
how.s3_html: A straight line from 0 to autostart_throttle (15 %) in autostart_ramp (10.0 s). The settings are frozen when the program starts.
how.s4_html: STEADY holds the level. GUSTS adds random sharp bursts between autostart_gust_min and autostart_gust_max. autostart_throttle_limit caps every output.
how.s5_html: DONE when autostart_run_time is over; LOW_BATTERY when the battery stays below cells × autostart_cell_cutoff (3.30 V per cell) for 5 s — then the ESC beeps every 3 s. With a run time of 0 it runs until the cut-off or power off.
how.stops_html:
• Opening the settings here, or the Betaflight CLI
  • The Motors tab of the Betaflight App
  • Arming with a receiver
  • A working receiver link (unless an RC switch is set)
  • Run time over
  • Battery low
  • Unplugging the battery
  • A button click while it runs
  • STOP on this page
how.stopsNote_html: It never restarts by itself. With the default start (Battery plugged in), plugging the battery in again starts the countdown again. After STOP, or once the settings were opened, the board waits until it is switched off and on: unplug USB and the battery, then plug in the battery. Every setting name, range and default: settings reference.
how.techStops_html: Setting names: the Motors tab sends MSP_SET_MOTOR; the RC switch is autostart_box; “Battery plugged in” is autostart_mode = POWER, the button is BUTTON.
how.techDefaults_html: Output: DShot300 by default (or PWM via motor_pwm_protocol). The first boot after flashing over another Betaflight resets all settings once; this build's defaults are the project settings (10 s wait, 10 s speed-up to 15 %). The configurator talks to the board over Web Serial (MSP).
wiring.title: Wiring: HGLRC F405 8S V2 + Flycolor X-Cross HV3 160A (6S)
wiring.lead: Use the 8-wire cable that comes with the flight controller (white ×4, yellow, green, black, red). Three joints, each soldered and insulated:
wiring.joints_html:
• ESC yellow (signal) → cable white next to the yellow (pin 1; in this build all four whites carry the same signal)
  • ESC black (signal ground) → cable black (G)
  • A new thin wire (22–24 AWG) from battery + → cable red (B, board power)
wiring.alt: Wiring diagram: the ESC's yellow signal wire goes to a white wire (pin 1) of the flight controller's 8-wire cable, the ESC's black wire to the cable's black (G), and a new wire from battery plus to the cable's red (B).
wiring.caption_html: Full pin map, the optional button and the first power-up checklist: docs/wiring.md.
wiring.notes_html:
• The cable's yellow is not the signal: it is the ESC telemetry input. Cut and insulate it, the green and the other whites.
  • Never more than 8S on B. For 10–12S, feed the board from a 12S-rated BEC.
  • Correct wiring: on battery the ESC plays 3 rising tones, then one low and one high tone (signal seen, armed).
support.title: Which computers and phones work
support.lead: The configurator talks to the board through Web Serial, a browser feature that only some browsers have.
support.r2w: Yes — asks once for a site permission (flashing firmware needs Chrome or Edge)
support.r3w: Only on phones whose Android has USB serial support (Google: “a limited set of devices”, from 2026) — try it
support.r4w: No — iOS browsers have no Web Serial or WebUSB
support.note_html: Only one program can use the board's port at a time: close the Betaflight App before connecting here, and this page before flashing.
safety.title: Risks and safety — read before you plug in a battery
safety.list_html:
• The motor starts by itself. With the default settings it spins 10 s after a battery is plugged in. Propeller off on the bench; treat a powered device as live.
  • Never more than 8S on the B pin. The red wire carries the battery voltage: if it touches a white, yellow or green wire, the flight controller's processor dies.
  • Ground use only. This is a motor driver, not a flight setup. Arming via a receiver hands the motors back to stock Betaflight.
  • The battery cut-off protects the pack, not the wiring. It is not a fuse, and with a cut-off of 0 there is none at all.
  • Some ESCs need PWM. A BLHeli_32 ESC that reports “activation failed” accepts PWM only: set motor_pwm_protocol = PWM.
  • Things outside this project can change: browser support for Web Serial, the Betaflight App, ESC firmware. If something stops working, tell me via Feedback.
faq.title: Questions people ask
faq.q1: How do I spin a brushless motor without a receiver or transmitter?
faq.a1_html: Flash Shramko Motor Autostart and plug in the battery: with the factory settings the motor waits 10 s, speeds up over 10 s to 15 % power and keeps running. No receiver, switch or computer is needed. Wait before start and Power are on the main panel of step 3 in the configurator, Speed-up time is in More settings → Start and power (CLI: autostart_delay, autostart_throttle, autostart_ramp).
faq.q2: Can Betaflight stop the motor when the LiPo is low?
faq.a2_html: Yes, from firmware 1.1, and it is on by default. Pick your pack under Battery on the main panel of step 3; the stop voltage per cell and the wait before the stop are in More settings → Battery. In the CLI: autostart_cells (6) and autostart_cell_cutoff (330 = 3.30 V per cell, 19.8 V on 6S). When the voltage stays below that for autostart_cutoff_time (5 s, so a short sag during a gust is ignored), the motor stops and, with DShot, beeps every 3 s. It starts again only after the battery is unplugged and plugged back in.
faq.q3: Does it work on Android or iPhone?
faq.a3_html: iPhone and iPad: no — no iOS browser has Web Serial or WebUSB (even Betaflight’s own iOS app connects only over Bluetooth). Android: Chrome 148+ with a USB-OTG cable, on phones whose Android supports USB serial; Google rolls this out to a limited set of devices, so just try it. On Windows, macOS and Linux use Chrome, Edge or Opera (or Firefox 151+).
faq.a4_html: A ready .hex exists for the HGLRC F405 8S V2 (HGLRC_F405_S8), tested with a Flycolor X-Cross HV3 160A (BLHeli_32) on 6S. Any other Betaflight board works after a build from source: add #define USE_AUTOSTART to the board's config.h and run the Docker build described in the README.
faq.q5: How do I make a slow soft start for an ESC, like 0 to 15 % over 10 seconds?
faq.a5_html: Set Power on the main panel of step 3 and Speed-up time in More settings → Start and power. In the CLI that is autostart_throttle in percent and autostart_ramp in tenths of a second (100 = 10.0 s, up to 600 s). The speed-up is a straight line: measured on hardware, it deviates by at most 1 µs.
faq.q6: Can I change the settings without this website?
faq.a6_html: Yes. In the Betaflight CLI, get autostart lists them, set autostart_throttle = 80 changes one, and save stores it and reboots. Entering the CLI stops a running program, so the motor never jumps to a new value.
faq.q7: Is it safe to plug in the battery while the USB cable is connected?
faq.a7_html: Yes, that is how bench tests are meant to be done (propeller off): the countdown starts only when the battery appears, unplugging it for more than 0.5 s stops the motor, and the CLI or the Motors tab takes over at once. If the motor should never spin while a computer is attached, choose Keep the motor stopped in More settings → Outputs and USB (CLI: autostart_usb_inhibit = ON).
faq.q8: How do I go back to normal Betaflight?
faq.a8_html: In the configurator, set What starts the motor to Off in More settings → Start and power: the module then stays idle and the board behaves like stock Betaflight (CLI: autostart_mode = OFF). Or flash …_stock.hex from the release — the same Betaflight 2025.12.1 without the module — or any official Betaflight build.
faq.q9: I saved my settings — why doesn't the motor start?
faq.a9_html: That is on purpose: opening the settings pauses the program, so nothing spins while you change things, and the board keeps it paused after saving. Press Run now… under the save message or Run the program… in Motor status — or switch the board off and on: unplug USB and the battery, then plug in the battery. Entering the Betaflight CLI pauses it the same way.
agent.title: For your AI agent
agent.p: Using Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor? Copy this prompt: it points your agent to the firmware, the settings and the safety rules.
agent.prompt:
Task: set up Shramko Motor Autostart (Betaflight 2025.12.1 firmware: the motor starts by itself on power-up, no receiver).
Repo: https://github.com/AndriiShramko/shramko-betaflight-motor-autostart - read AGENT_SETUP.md and docs/settings.md first.
1. Ask me to remove the propeller. Never let the motor spin with a propeller on.
2. Firmware: the .hex from https://github.com/AndriiShramko/shramko-betaflight-motor-autostart/releases/latest (HGLRC F405 8S V2 = HGLRC_F405_S8). Other Betaflight boards: build from source (README, Docker, #define USE_AUTOSTART in the board's config.h).
3. Flash: https://app.betaflight.com in Chrome or Edge -> Firmware Flasher -> Load Firmware [Local] -> Flash Firmware. Windows "DFU device not found": ImpulseRC Driver Fixer or Zadig (WinUSB for STM32 BOOTLOADER).
4. Configure: https://autostart.flyreelstudio.eu (Connect, Change settings, Save to board) or the Betaflight CLI: get autostart / set autostart_<name> = <value> / save. Use only the names, ranges and defaults in docs/settings.md.
5. Wiring: docs/wiring.md. Never more than 8S on pin B.

contact.title: Who made this, and working together
contact.role: Drones · 360° camera rigs for extreme shoots · 3D/4D Gaussian splatting · Bydgoszcz, Poland
contact.p1: I'm Andrii Shramko. I build drone and 360° camera systems for extreme shoots — storm chasing, city-scale Gaussian-splat scans — and the tools around them. This firmware drives the blower of the META4 Tornado camera case: it clears water from the 360° camera's optics as soon as the box is powered, with nobody touching it.
contact.open: Open to interesting people and ready to help teams build ambitious projects — embedded and drone hardware, camera rigs, scanning pipelines, partnerships, licensing or funding.
lead.title: Write to me
lead.consent: I agree that Andrii Shramko stores my email and message to reply to me (see Privacy below).
lead.hint: To send: pick who you are, add a valid email and tick the consent.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.p1: Controller: Andrii Shramko, Bydgoszcz, Poland — zmei116@gmail.com. The configurator talks to your flight controller directly from your browser: the board's settings and live data never reach our server.
privacy.p2: The server stores only what you send on purpose: feedback (bug, idea) and collaboration messages, with a contact if you give one, and — only if you tick the box — technical details (page version, browser and screen, recent errors, the configurator's log). The text and the contact are also forwarded to the author's Telegram (Telegram FZ-LLC, Dubai — outside the EEA); the original stays on a server in the EU. Kept for up to 12 months and used only to reply and to fix the site.
privacy.p3: Page counters work without cookies and without IP addresses; the server logs keep no IP addresses and no query strings. Google Analytics is loaded only after you accept it.
privacy.p4: You can ask for a copy or deletion of your data at any time: zmei116@gmail.com.
